_README: Source-backed Rwanda crop catalogue for the FieldShift Kayonza pilot. Every duration/variety/constraint fact is tagged with provenance below. Where a figure in the underlying research was flagged as unverified or general (non-Rwanda-specific) agronomic knowledge, that caveat is carried into field_constraints/rotation_notes/provenance verbatim rather than silently treated as fact. This catalogue models ONE representative RAB-linked variety per crop for the Kayonza pilot demo; GAEZ evidence (gaez_adapter.py) is species-level and independent of variety choice, per Stage C guidance not to treat GAEZ species outputs as variety-specific predictions.

crops.variety_name: RHM1407 (RAB-linked hybrid; representative short-duration pilot variety)
planting_windows: Season A (national convention): planting Sept–Dec, harvest Jan–Feb
field_constraints: Eastern Province (incl. Kayonza) Season A rains are documented as shorter, later-onset and more erratic than the national pattern; RAB officials are quoted (2025) stating that if rain fails to arrive within ~3 weeks of planting, maize establishment is compromised in Kayonza/Kirehe.
Fall Armyworm (FAW, detected Rwanda 2017) and Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN) are documented, RAB-recognized risks nationally; RAB breeding programs target both as active priorities.

RHM1407's ~85-day duration and ~6 t/ha figure come from farmer/news reporting (AllAfrica/New Times, Jan 2026) of a RAB-linked variety-selection exercise, not a RAB variety-release datasheet directly retrieved — treated as credible but secondary-sourced.
crops.rotation_notes: Legume rotation (bean or soybean before maize) is documented Rwanda agronomic guidance: the legume should not receive N fertilizer itself; manure or half-manure/half-DAP should instead go to the following maize, which shows improved N/P uptake after a legume predecessor (Eastern Province-focused Kenyatta University thesis, found via search synthesis of the PDF, not independently re-read). IMPORTANT TIMING CAVEAT from the same source: in Bugesera (an Eastern Province area agronomically similar to Kayonza), maize planted after a long-duration soybean failed to yield any grain because the legume delayed maize planting too far into the dry period — i.e. in short-rain, erratic-onset Eastern Province conditions, the preceding legume's duration must leave enough of the rain window for maize, or the rotation can backfire.
crops.provenance: RAB Cereals Program (https://www.rab.gov.rw/1-1/news/cereals-program); AllAfrica 'Rwanda: Farmers Pick Climate-Smart Seeds That Double Yields' (Jan 2026, https://allafrica.com/stories/202601020015.html); MINAGRI FAW response (https://www.minagri.gov.rw/updates/news-details/government-intensifies-efforts-to-contain-fall-armyworms); UN Rwanda FAW monitoring (https://rwanda.un.org/en/node/3066); Meteo Rwanda Crop Monitor bulletins Sept/Dec 2021 (meteorwanda.gov.rw) documenting Kayonza-specific late-rain damage to maize; AllAfrica Sept 2025 Kayonza farmer/RAB quotes on short-cycle drought-tolerant variety need (https://allafrica.com/stories/202509030320.html, read via search-engine summary — direct fetch returned HTTP 403).

crops.variety_name: RWV 3006 (RAB-released 2012; bush-type assumed, growth habit not independently confirmed)
planting_windows: Season A (national convention): planting Sept–Dec, harvest Jan–Feb
field_constraints: No Kayonza-specific bean planting window distinct from the national Season A/B dates was found in sources; the national window is used with the same Eastern Province late/erratic-onset caveat documented for maize in the same Dec 2021 Crop Monitor bulletin (which reports BOTH maize and bean crops in Kayonza affected by late rainfall/dry weather during germination/vegetative growth).

Documented Rwanda-relevant bean disease constraints: Angular Leaf Spot, bean root rot, anthracnose, Common Bacterial Blight, Bean Common Mosaic Virus/BCMNV — RAB's Rwerere station is used as an anthracnose resistance-screening hotspot.

RWV3006's 120-day duration is drawn from a peer-reviewed table (Agriculture & Food Security journal) stating it sourced maturity/release data from official RAB release records — the strongest-provenance duration figure found for any single Rwandan bean variety. Growth habit (bush vs climbing) for RWV3006 was NOT independently confirmed.

Faster alternatives exist in the catalogue literature but with weaker provenance: RWV2070 and RWV3316 are both reported at 110 days (same journal table); a 2021 RAB/CIAT/PABRA release of 19 new varieties (13 climbing, 6 bush) exists but individual variety names/durations for that batch could not be found in any source checked.
crops.rotation_notes: Common bean fixes atmospheric nitrogen and should not be top-dressed with N fertilizer; Rwanda guidance directs manure/DAP to the following cereal instead. Rotation with a cereal (maize) is documented as helping break pest/disease cycles for both crops. Maize-bean rotation/intercropping is widely described as common Rwandan practice, but no single official RAB/FAO document spelling out exact spacing/timing protocol was located — the rotation *rationale* is well-sourced, the precise agronomic protocol is not.
crops.provenance: RAB 'RAB Launches 19 New Varieties of Beans' (https://www.rab.gov.rw/1-1/news-details/rab-launches-19-new-varieties-of-beans); CGIAR release summary (https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/farmer-preferred-market-demanded-and-highly-nutritious-beans-to-boost-rwandas-household-diets-and-wealth); Agriculture & Food Security journal, Table 4 of PPB trial variety characteristics citing official RAB release data (https://agricultureandfoodsecurity.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s40066-016-0062-8/tables/4); Crop Trust/CIAT genebank impact brief on CAB2-derived Rwandan bean pedigrees; Meteo Rwanda Crop Monitor bulletin December 2021 (Kayonza bean/maize late-rain impact); MSU Legume Lab Technical Progress Report (bean disease constraints, https://www.canr.msu.edu/legumelab/uploads/files/MSU-1%20Tech%20Prog%20Rpt%20FY11%20Final.pdf).
